Rules for running the agent's playbooks

The rules for running the agent's playbooks decide which fixes the triage agent may run without a person's approval.

Services whose changes a person must approve

On every inventory, a playbook with a task that starts, stops, restarts, or changes a listed systemd service waits for a person, whatever the rules of its kinds of action below, unless the playbook is listed by name below:

  • pgautofailover.service

MMHotline cannot check a service against the list when the service name is known only when the playbook runs. A person must approve the playbook.

Changed 13:45 by the settings file.

The inventory “production”

MMHotline's copy of the systems repository has no inventories/production.yml.

  • Start or restart a serviceAct, then reportChanged 13:45 by the settings file
  • Free disk spaceAct, then reportChanged 13:45 by the settings file
  • Pull a container image againAct, then reportChanged 13:45 by the settings file
  • Reboot a serverGet permission, then act (1 approval)Changed 13:45 by the settings file
  • Block a network rangeGet permission, then act (1 approval)Changed 13:45 by the settings file
  • Change DNS recordsGet permission, then act (1 approval)Changed 13:45 by the settings file
  • Check onlyAct, then reportChanged 13:45 by the settings file
  • Unrecognized taskGet permission, then act (1 approval)Changed 13:45 by the settings file
What MMHotline counts as each kind of action

Each playbook uses the strictest rule among the playbook's kinds of action.

MMHotline reads each task of a playbook from mmx explain, never from the playbook's name or the agent's words, and sorts each task into a kind of action. A task is of a kind only when all of these hold: - the task's module is one of MMX's core modules listed below, not a module of the team's own or an official extra module; - mmx explain lists the task as ready: MMX knows before the run that the task runs, which a when usually prevents; - the task writes no argument outside its module's list; - each value a condition reads is known before the run: not a secret and not another task's result. Each task inside a role or a task block is sorted by itself. Every other task is an Unrecognized task, and so is each file a fleet stage saves on MMHotline's server with save_on_controller_machine.

Start or restart a service

  • systemd_service. Arguments: name, state, restart_now, run_only_once_marker_file, in_systemd_of_user_account. Conditions: systemd_service.name must be a plain service of the team's, known before the run: a name ending in .service or with no unit type, with only letters, digits, and _ . -, and not a template instance (@), a systemd-* or dbus-org.* unit, or an operating system unit whose start shuts down, reboots, opens a shell, changes the network or firewall, or installs updates, such as poweroff, reboot, emergency, networking, or apt-daily-upgrade; systemd_service.state must be running; systemd_service.restart_now must be true or false; systemd_service.restart_now: true requires run_only_once_marker_file; systemd_service.run_only_once_marker_file must be known before the run and name a file directly in /var/lib/mmx/commands_run_once/, whose name has only letters, digits, and _ . -: MMX writes the marker file as root, so a marker elsewhere, such as /etc/nologin, could lock people out.
    - systemd_service:
    name: caddy
    state: running
    restart_now: true
    run_only_once_marker_file: /var/lib/mmx/commands_run_once/2026-11-03_restart_caddy

Free disk space

  • systemd_journal_vacuum. Arguments: keep_at_most_size, keep_newer_than. Conditions: systemd_journal_vacuum.keep_newer_than must be at least 1d, known before the run: the journal is the evidence of an incident; systemd_journal_vacuum.keep_at_most_size must be at least 100MiB, known before the run: a smaller journal holds only hours of a busy server's logs, the evidence of an incident.
    - systemd_journal_vacuum:
    keep_at_most_size: 500MiB
  • podman_unused_images. Arguments: remove, in_image_store_of_user_account. Conditions: podman_unused_images.remove must be dangling_images_only: every_image_no_container_uses also removes named images, such as a previous version kept for a rollback or an image built on the server, which can be the only copy.
    - podman_unused_images:
    remove: dangling_images_only
  • docker_unused_images. Arguments: remove, in_image_store_of_user_account. Conditions: docker_unused_images.remove must be dangling_images_only: every_image_no_container_uses also removes named images, such as a previous version kept for a rollback or an image built on the server, which can be the only copy.
    - docker_unused_images:
    remove: dangling_images_only
  • apt_downloaded_package_files. Arguments: state. Conditions: apt_downloaded_package_files.state must be absent.
    - apt_downloaded_package_files:
    state: absent
  • delete_old_files. Arguments: directory, name_patterns, older_than, include_subdirectories. Conditions: delete_old_files.directory must be /var/log itself (include_subdirectories: true also selects log directories below /var/log); delete_old_files.older_than must be at least 1d: a fresh log is the evidence of an incident; delete_old_files.name_patterns must be only rotated-log patterns (*.gz, *.xz, *.zst, *.bz2, *.[0-9], *.[0-9].gz, *.old): a live log that a process has open frees no space when deleted.
    - delete_old_files:
    directory: /var/log
    name_patterns: ["*.gz", "*.[0-9]"]
    older_than: 7d
    include_subdirectories: true

Pull a container image again

  • podman_image. Arguments: image, pull_image, registry_username, registry_password, in_image_store_of_user_account. Conditions: podman_image.pull_image must be always; podman_image.image, registry_username, and registry_password must be known before the run, so not a secret: Podman sends the login to the registry that image names, which the playbook chooses.
    - podman_image:
    image: registry.example.com/shop/web:2.4
    pull_image: always

Reboot a server

  • reboot. Arguments: skip_if_this_path_exists, run_only_if_this_path_exists, wait_at_most.
    - reboot:
    wait_at_most: 10m

Block a network range

  • ufw. Arguments: state, incoming_rules_not_listed, incoming_rules. Conditions: ufw.state must be present or left out; ufw.incoming_rules_not_listed must be keep; ufw.incoming_rules must give each rule an action of deny or reject and a from value; only protocol and incoming_interface may also be set, so port and from_inventory_group are not allowed.
    - ufw:
    incoming_rules_not_listed: keep
    incoming_rules:
      - action: deny
        protocol: tcp_and_udp
        from: 203.0.113.0/24

Change DNS records

  • http. Arguments: url, method, headers, json_body, body, expected_http_status_codes, changed_when. Conditions: http.url must be https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/ZONE_ID/dns_records or a path below the zone's dns_records path, with no .. part and no escaped character; http.headers must be known before the run and must not set Host: a Host header asks Cloudflare's servers for another site, which would receive the team's token; http.json_body and body must be known before the run, so not a secret: a DNS record's content is public.
    - http:
    url: https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/ID-1/dns_records/ID-2
    method: PATCH
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer {{ .secrets.cloudflare_api_token }}"
    json_body:
      content: 198.51.100.4

Check only

  • assert. Arguments: that, message.
    - assert:
    that:
      equals: ["{{ .node.distribution.id }}", debian]
    message: This fix is written for Debian.
  • wait_for. Arguments: tcp_port_accepts_connections, tcp_port_refuses_connections, tcp_host, path_exists, path_is_missing, url_responds, trusted_certificate_authority_file, dangerously_skip_server_certificate_check, docker_container_is_healthy, docker_compose_project_is_ready, podman_container_is_healthy, podman_container_of_user_account, expected_http_status_codes, response_body_contains, wait_at_most. Conditions: wait_for.url_responds and tcp_host must be known before the run, so not a secret: the server connects to the host they name, which the playbook chooses.
    - wait_for:
    url_responds: http://127.0.0.1:8080/
    wait_at_most: 60s
  • show. Arguments: any.
    - show: Caddy answers again.
  • set_vars. Arguments: any.
    - set_vars:
    restarted_service: caddy
  • role. Arguments: any.
  • task_block. Arguments: any.
Where the rules are set

Set in TEMPORARY-DIRECTORY/mmhotline_settings.yml, in rules_for_running_agent_playbooks and services_whose_changes_a_person_must_approve. The file's first line says: Managed by MMX from mmhotline_settings.yml in the systems repository. Change it there and push; util01 applies it.

Times are New York time (America/New_York), the team's time zone.
